transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-29 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees listed above

Summary:
Quick procurement + legal alignment on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA tiering options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), pricing approval path and a technical benchmark to validate latency and egress estimates. Actionable next steps captured at the end.

Topics:
- MSA/DPA redline expectations and exceptions
- SLA commitment levels and latency/throughput targets for pilot vs GA
- Data residency and KMS/HSM obligations
- Billing/pricing approval workflow and procurement timeline
- Technical benchmark scope and owner

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining um we'll run through the onboarding playbook and focus on the contract and SLA bits first. quick roll call?
[00:08] Lina (Orchid): lina here, marcus, aisha, tom on my side.
[00:12] Marcus (Orchid/CISO): Marcus here.
[00:14] Aisha (Orchid/Legal): Aisha here.
[00:16] Tom (Orchid/Platform): Tom joining.
[00:18] Priya (Redwood): Priya here from SE. hi all.
[00:20] Jordan: awesome. quick agenda: we want to align on the MSA/DPA redlines you flagged in the intake doc, confirm which SLA tier you want for pilot (we generally see e.g., standard hosted tier vs dedicated pool with SLOs), go over data residency/KMS constraints, and then book the benchmarking.

[00:38] Lina: to give context, procurement needs a clear approval path — our finance and security teams need to sign off. the procurement deadline is end of Q2 but legal wants to get redlines early. also pricing approvals need to be routed through our central purchasing system.

[00:55] Jordan: understood. on the pricing side we'll provide a pricing card and a committed capacity path if you want reserved/dedicated GPUs which gives predictable throughput. that usually helps finance with forecasting.

[01:08] Aisha: thanks. on the DPA/msa: we have three main asks — stronger audit rights, a narrow subprocessor list, and KMS control for customer keys. we also have a clause about data return/destruction that we want explicit timelines for.

[01:28] Priya: yeah on the KMS we support customer-managed keys via our private deployment and also KMS integrations in the hosted flow for enterprise plans. small caveat is on hosted we use a Redwood-managed HSM unless you opt for the private package.

[01:45] Tom: can you clarify hosted vs private exactly — like what network topology and egress possibilities? we need to know whether traffic can stay within our VPC and how egress billing shows up.

[01:58] Priya: great q. hosted is a Redwood-managed endpoint in our cloud, it's easiest to onboard but data crosses Redwood-managed infra (we do at-rest encryption and TLS in transit). dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools inside a tenant boundary with stronger isolation and predictable throughput. private (VPC/on-prem) gives you customer-managed networking and KMS — that's what most regulated customers take. egress billing differs: hosted charges per token/embedding plus possible data transfer fees; dedicated commits reduce unit price. we'll send the sheet with examples.

[02:33] Marcus: from a security POV our must-haves are: SOC2 + ISO references, audit logs that we can pull, SSO/SAML integration with RBAC, and option for customer KMS. also we need retention controls and to know retention defaults.

[02:50] Jordan: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II, and we can provide certs. audit logs and token-level traces are available in the Console. SSO/SAML is supported — we'll include our SAML integration guide. retention defaults are 30 days for ephemeral logs unless you choose extended retention for an add-on; we'll confirm the exact retention buckets.

[03:12] Aisha: on the MSA — indemnity caps and limitation of liability are sensitive. we need to know if Redwood will accept mutual caps and whether there are carve-outs for willful misconduct. also the warranty language around model hallucination risk — we want clearer language that limits liability for model outputs.

[03:35] Jordan: typical approach is mutual caps with exceptions for gross negligence/willful misconduct; for model outputs we include language that the customer controls prompts and use cases and that Redwood doesn't guarantee factual correctness of model output. we can propose a customer-friendly clause but procurement/legal teams often accept the standard. we'll send a redline.

[03:52] Lina: about SLAs — for the pilot we only need a baseline: 95th percentile p95 latency target and 99.9% uptime for the API. if we move to a production tier, we'll consider the dedicated SLA with stricter SLOs. can you provide examples of observed p95 for generative workloads?

[04:10] Priya: yes, we'll attach a latency snapshot. for our hosted LLM catalog p95 for a 1k token request varies by model and sequence length; typical numbers are 350-650 ms for shorter sequences, but long-form can be multiple seconds. with dedicated GPU pools and quantized weights we can get down to low hundreds consistently. caveat: your prompt engineering and batching strategy matters.

[04:36] Tom: we plan to do health records redaction in the pipeline before sending to the model, so we want to confirm that partial tokenization or KV cache won't leak anything. is there any caching behavior that keeps PII?

[04:49] Priya: Redwood's prefix/KV cache operates per-session and can be configured not to persist beyond the request; for private deployments you can disable caching or configure TTLs. we'll document defaults. apologies if previous notes said "K-V cash" in the intake, that was a mis-transcription.

[05:06] Marcus: auditability is key. can logs be exported into our SIEM and do they include per-request user identifiers?

[05:15] Jordan: yes export via syslog or API; logs include request IDs, model/version, token counts, and configured metadata. PII fields are not emitted by default unless you pass them. we'll share a log schema sample.

[05:28] Aisha: procurement asked about termination assistance — if we end the contract what's the data return timeline and any fees?

[05:36] Jordan: standard is 90 days to return data unless otherwise negotiated, and we can include assisted export as a paid service. we can talk specifics on the redline.

[05:44] Lina: pricing approvals: we have a two-step path, finance needs a committed cost estimate (including possible reserved/dedicated cost) and procurement needs to see MSA redlines. is there an approvals cadence on your side?

[05:55] Jordan: typically we provide a proposal and a committed-cost appendix for dedicated capacity. our pricing team will work with procurement after legal aligns on MSA. we can provide a tiered pricing card and an example committed contract.

[06:08] Tom: on technical validation — we want to run a benchmark that mirrors our traffic, with the same prompt lengths and concurrency. who owns the benchmark and what does Redwood need from us?

[06:18] Priya: Redwood SEs will run the benchmark alongside your team — we'll need a representative traffic trace (RPS, average tokens, peak concurrency) and a few sample prompts. timeline: we can run a 2-hour benchmark and deliver a results sheet within 3 business days.

[06:33] Marcus: any export controls or geo restrictions we should be aware of? our data residency is EU-first for this workload.

[06:40] Jordan: EU regions are supported for Private deployments and some hosted model endpoints; we can show which models and regions are available. for controlled data we recommend private or dedicated with regional tenancy.

[06:54] Aisha: about subprocessors — can you provide a narrow list and commit to notification of changes?

[07:01] Jordan: yes we publish a subprocessor list and commit to 30-day notice for material changes. we'll include that in the DPA addendum.

[07:10] Lina: ok let's recap next steps.
[07:14] Jordan: recap - Jordan sends annotated MSA + DPA redlines; Priya sends latency/cost workbook and sample SLA cards; Tom provides traffic profile; Aisha provides non-starter clauses and residency constraints; schedule a 2 hour benchmark in mid-April.

[07:30] Evan (Redwood CSM): i'll coordinate calendar invites and follow up on the intake checklist.
[07:36] Aisha: quick Q — if we choose dedicated for pilot do you offer short-term commitments?
[07:41] Jordan: yes short-term reserved windows are available (monthly commits) and you can bump to annual for lower unit costs. we'll put examples in the pricing sheet.
[07:52] Tom: one last technical: can we limit model versions and pin weights to avoid silent upgrades during pilot?
[07:57] Priya: yes you can pin model versions and we support rollout controls. there is a model catalog with versioning and rollback.
[08:06] Jordan: great, thanks all. we'll get the materials out this week and follow up on due dates. appreciate the time.
[08:14] Lina: thanks everyone. bye.

End of transcript.
